options: The program finds the greatest common divisor K of two positive integers I and J.

model_outputs:

question: Which one of the following is equal to P(A, B, C) given Boolean random variables A, B and C, and no independence or conditional independence assumptions between any of them?
options: P(A, B | C) * P(C | A, B)
P(A | B) * P(B | C) * P(C)
P(C | A, B) * P(A) * P(B)
P(A, B | C) * P(C)
P(A | B, C) * P(B) * P(C)
P(A | B) * P(B | C) * P(C | A, B)
P(A | B, C) * P(B | A, C) * P(C | A, B)
P(A, B) * P(B, C) * P(C, A)
P(A | B) * P(B | C) * P(C | A)
P(A, B, C | D) * P(D)
model_outputs:
The correct answer is:
P(A, B, C) = P(A, B) * P(B, C) * P(C).
We can verify this by calculating P(A, B, C) separately. We know that P(A, B) = P(B, A) = P(C, A) = p. So we can plug these values into the formula to get P(A, B, C) = p^3.

II. G has a vertex with no outgoing edge.
III. G has an isolated vertex, that is, one with neither an incoming edge nor an outgoing edge.
options: I and III only
None of the above
I and II only
II and III only
I, II, and a vertex with one outgoing edge
I, II, and a vertex with one incoming edge
All of the above (I, II, III)
II only
I only
III only
model_outputs: Option (G) is correct. For a graph to have a cycle, it must have an edge from a vertex to itself. Therefore, if a graph has any isolated vertices (vertices with no incoming or outgoing edges), it will have a cycle.
